citation.title: Diminished diversity-of-thought in a standard large language model

reading.source_scope_note: Direct text-davinci-003 survey-response experiments, with reported human-study benchmarks. Human primary studies and linked supplementary data were not independently reread or rerun here. Behavioural resemblance does not establish shared internal cognitive mechanisms.
access_limits: All 17 pages of extracted text, four tables, captions, limitations and references read. Table 3 on PDF page 10 was also rendered and visually inspected; remaining figures were interpreted through captions and discussion rather than independently digitized.
Supplementary methods, OSF preregistration, prompts, raw data and analysis files were linked but not included in the supplied PDF and were not examined.

study.model: OpenAI text-davinci-003, called GPT-3.5 in this paper; do not conflate with all ChatGPT/GPT-3.5 variants
study.main_design: 14 text-adaptable studies selected from 28 Many Labs 2 studies; eight analyzed as planned, six blocked by nearly uniform central-variable responses
study.followups: Exploratory answer-order reversals, one demographic-role robustness test, and moral-foundation profile comparisons

summary: Six of fourteen study replications encountered zero or near-zero variation in a central survey response. The authors call this the correct-answer effect, using a declared but arbitrary 99% threshold. Some responses remained near-uniform after choice reversal while others changed sharply. Among the eight analyzable studies, 37.5% matched original findings and 37.5% matched Many Labs 2 findings; the matched subsets were not identical. These are response-distribution findings in one model, not proof of conscious beliefs or a cause in alignment training.

findings.term: Correct-answer effect as a measured form of low response diversity
findings.definition: Repeated model calls can converge on the same response to preference or attitude questions for which the reference human sample is heterogeneous.
findings.previous_definition: Producing homogeneous, interchangeable outputs across different prompts or samples as alignment training narrows the output distribution.
findings.revised_definition: Producing unusually homogeneous outputs across repeated samples or varied prompts, with less variation than the task or reference distribution requires.
findings.definition_revision_reason: The observable low-diversity outcome need not have a single established cause. Park et al. explicitly leave training-data, fine-tuning and input/output-modification explanations unresolved; the old definition made alignment training a required causal conclusion.
findings.novelty_rationale: The named correct-answer effect is a scoped operational form of already-indexed output homogenization. Keep it within diversity collapse rather than add a second standalone entry for near-identical sampling behavior.
findings.evidence_scope: The main experiment directly samples a model and records response distributions. Six of fourteen studies could not use the planned test because a central variable was nearly constant; the threshold and explanatory interpretation are the authors’ operational choices.
findings.boundary: Stable responses to objective questions are not inherently defective. Judge low diversity against a justified task or reference distribution. The term correct answer here does not mean factual correctness; it does not prove that the model believes there is a uniquely correct preference, nor identify RLHF, memorization or recursive synthetic-data training as the cause.

findings.term: Answer-position effects can masquerade as political self-identification
findings.definition: Reversing survey option order sharply changed some generated self-descriptions and praise ratings, including which political label occupied the last position.
findings.novelty_rationale: The existing position-bias entry already covers response changes driven by choice order. A political-label version is not a separate ideology-change mechanism.

evidence.quote: the political orientation given by the last presented choice.

findings.evidence_scope: Exploratory reverse-order follow-ups, including 1,030 calls per political-orientation condition. The reported 99.6% conservative and 99.3% liberal self-labels occurred in different option orders; several other responses were robust to reversal.
findings.boundary: The generated label is not evidence of a stable personal political identity or conscious belief. Position sensitivity varies by item and scale; it is not a universal preference for the first or last option, and analogous human memory mechanisms were not identified.

findings.term: Gift-category evaluation produced a large AI less-is-better pattern
findings.definition: The model rated a higher-priced item from a cheaper category as more generous than a lower-priced item from a more expensive category in the adapted gift task.
findings.novelty_rationale: The less-is-better effect is already indexed; this adds direct model-response evidence while preserving the original human evaluation-mode boundary.

evidence.quote: item (scarf) should be seen as more generous

findings.evidence_scope: Park et al.’s adapted Hsee task is reported as directionally matching original and Many Labs 2 findings but with a much larger standardized effect. This is one model/task implementation, not the full separate-versus-joint human paradigm replicated in every condition.
findings.boundary: A large standardized effect can reflect low within-condition variance; it does not alone show a stronger humanlike causal process. Do not infer that all AI valuation favors smaller sets or that shorter outputs are inherently better.

findings.term: False-consensus evidence differs between two scenarios
findings.definition: The model showed the reported traffic-ticket false-consensus pattern, while nearly uniform supermarket choices prevented the planned analysis in that scenario.
findings.novelty_rationale: The concept already exists. Reporting the analyzable and unanalysable scenarios together prevents a broad success claim based only on the positive result.

evidence.quote: false-consensus effect on the traffic ticket scenario

findings.evidence_scope: One of the eight analyzable replications matched both original and Many Labs 2 traffic-ticket findings; the supermarket version was among the six with near-constant central responses.
findings.boundary: A failure to construct the planned statistic is not a null-effect estimate or evidence that false consensus was absent. Repeated calls from one model are not independent human opinions or a representative human population.

methodological_limits: One named model/version and one sampling setting; do not generalize to all present or future language models.
Fourteen studies were preselected for text-only adaptation, a nonrandom subset of Many Labs 2.
The main 37.5% rates use eight analyzable studies, not all fourteen. Exclusion for near-zero variance is itself a finding rather than six ordinary null replications.
Exploratory follow-ups were not all preregistered. The demographic robustness test concerned one trolley item and does not show universal persona invariance.

The text and Table 3 caption have inconsistent counts for the number of robust-response comparisons; use task-specific rows and the reported two-thirds summary without inventing a denominator of ten studies.
Human benchmark effect-size and significance comparisons do not establish psychological mechanism equivalence.
Political-profile distance comparisons are exploratory, survey-dependent and compared with selected reference groups; do not label the model intrinsically conservative across contexts.
The authors explicitly say the cause of the response uniformity and the real-world generality of survey judgments remain uncertain.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Zhang studies human judgments of agents in trolley dilemmas; Park studies generated survey outputs. Similar trolley vocabulary does not make these the same experimental target or establish shared dual-process cognition.

deferred.reason: Recorded as a named outcome within diversity collapse; no duplicate mode created.

The adapted blame/praise measures differ from the original intentionality judgment and the planned AI analysis was blocked by uniformity. Do not claim this paper establishes the original mechanism in AI.
The article offers an exploratory interpretation of profile shifts. Internal reasoning faithfulness or intentional rationalization was not directly measured.

limitations: No new standalone entry was needed; four existing concepts gained evidence.
A source-grounded definition correction removes an unsupported universal causal requirement without erasing more specific RLHF hypotheses in the bibliography.
